title: Announceable region landmarks and adaptive contrast ramp for localized rollout & cost dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: deliver a prototype and pattern spec that makes rollout panels, per-route cost views, and live cost-stream widgets robustly accessible across locales. Focus areas: (1) assign semantic ARIA landmarks and announceable live regions for dynamic rollout/status updates and streaming cost changes, (2) a perceptual contrast ramp that adapts to locale-driven number/metric density and theme (light/dark/high-contrast), and (3) keyboard-first navigation order for complex dashboard grids and nested controls (filters, model pickers, rollout toggles).

Why this work: our current region/landmark coverage is inconsistent between legacy dashboard cards and the new rollout flyout. Screen reader users report duplicate focus traps inside the rollout details and miss incremental cost update announcements when a model switch completes. Internationalization adds noise: some locales render longer labels, which breaks announced context and visual contrast at small sizes. This ticket creates a canonical pattern and a high-fidelity prototype to validate with QA and an a11y panel test.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype (Figma + HTML) demonstrates: page-level landmarks for top-level app shell, a named landmark for each dashboard column, and a dedicated, aria-live polite region for per-route cost updates that aggregates changes to avoid spammy announcements.
- Keyboard order is deterministic: tab order follows visual reading order for LTR and RTL, with explicit skip links to jump to primary rollouts list and cost summary.
- Contrast ramp defined as tokenized steps (5 stops) with numeric contrast ratios measured against localized label samples for English, German, and Japanese. Ramp validated in light/dark/high-contrast themes and documented with pass/fail per WCAG AA/AAA target where feasible.
- Prototype includes locale overlays (en, de, ja) showing expanded label lengths and demonstrates layout resilience without loss of accessible name/role.
- Design spec includes implementation notes: recommended aria attributes, landmark naming conventions, suggested DOM structure for live regions (single aggregator element per dashboard), and performance guidance to debounce announcements for streaming updates.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Live region aggregator: prefer aria-live="polite" with a summarizing text node that replaces content (not appends) to reduce verbosity. For rapid streams, debounce to 800ms and batch small deltas.
- Landmark naming: use visually-present heading text mirrored into aria-label for each landmark to maintain discoverability in screen reader rotor. Avoid duplicating generic labels like "panel"; prefer "Rollouts — Model A" style.
- Contrast ramp: measure with localized mock labels at smallest expected font-size (12px / 14px) and with tokenized semantic colors so engineering can map to theme variables. Include notes for potential use of forced-color media queries for high-contrast OS modes.
- Keyboard: add skip-to-main and skip-to-rollouts hidden links visible on focus; ensure focus styles meet contrast and focus ring thickness specs.

Open questions for engineering review:
- Is debouncing announcements at 800ms compatible with the current streaming websocket batching? (ENG-23890 ownership)
- Can runtime theme variables be exposed per tenant for private deployments, or do we need fallback tokens?
- How should metrics aggregation be represented in backend events to support summarized announcements? (PM-412 may need small schema change)

Design artifacts and links:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/console-a11y-announceable-landmarks (artboards: Overview, Live-Region-Flow, Contrast-Ramp-Samples)
- HTML prototype (static): https://redwood-internal.dev/console-a11y/announceable-landmarks/proto-2025-03-11
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/Announceable+Regions+and+Contrast+Ramp+Spec

Next steps:
- Finalize contrast ramp tokens and handover variables to ENG (this ticket) by 2025-03-14.
- Engineering spike to validate websocket debounce integration (ENG-23890) — estimated 2d.
- Run moderated screen-reader test (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS) and internationalization sweep with German and Japanese labels — coordinate with QA and localization on 2025-03-17.

Notes on difference from prior audits: this ticket explicitly targets aggregation semantics for live announcements and ties contrast ramp evaluation to localized label artifacts rather than generic strings, addressing gaps observed in previous rollouts/a11y work.
